entries.topic: results evidence findings confidence inconclusive verification
entries.title: What LyraShield result states mean
entries.content: Detected means a check found evidence of a possible issue. Verified requires independent evidence; model confidence alone is not verification. Inconclusive means the available evidence cannot establish a reliable result. No finding means an assigned check found no mapped issue within its scope, not that an application is universally safe. Evidence required means operational or human proof is still needed. A clean scan is not a security guarantee.

entries.topic: free lite check public website passive scanner
entries.title: What the free Lite Check does
entries.content: Lite Check is a passive outside-in review of one public HTTP or HTTPS page, response headers, and up to six same-origin linked assets. It checks basic HTTPS, mixed content, headers, CORS, framework markers and high-confidence secret patterns without returning matched values. It does not authenticate, exploit, fuzz, brute-force, crawl arbitrary paths or produce the official LyraShield Score. Only submit targets you own or are authorized to test.

entries.topic: free browser local security tools privacy files
entries.title: Browser-local security tools
entries.content: The public Tools area includes browser-local security utilities. Selected files and pasted code stay in the browser for those utilities; they are not a full repository scan and do not create persistent evidence, retests or assurance reports. Read each tool's coverage and limits before relying on its result.

entries.topic: create account sign up login onboarding workspace
entries.title: Create an account and start
entries.content: Registration is open. Create a verified account, choose or create a workspace, add an authorized target and select an available review depth. The dashboard shows the next action and recent activity. A workspace switch changes the scope of targets, scans and findings you see; it does not change permissions or scan behavior.

entries.topic: repository github URL API target asset authorization
entries.title: Choose and add a scan target
entries.content: Targets represent an authorized repository, web application URL or API. Add a target in the dashboard before starting a scan. A GitHub-connected repository requires the approved GitHub App installation and ownership validation. URL and API review requires current domain verification. Choose the target type and review depth that match what you are authorized to test.

entries.topic: start scan new scan queue worker unavailable status refresh cancel
entries.title: Start and monitor a scan
entries.content: Open Trust Runs, choose New Scan, select a target and available review depth, then Start Scan. Only one active scan may run on the same target. The scan list shows queued, preflight, running, verifying and terminal states and has Refresh and Cancel actions. If the scan worker is unavailable, no scan is created; wait briefly and retry once.

entries.topic: scan results details manifest coverage receipts events limitations
entries.title: Read scan details and coverage
entries.content: A scan detail shows status, target, review depth, completed scanner scope, summary, coverage warnings, retained findings and the event timeline. Repository scans also show the selected model and reasoning effort. The result manifest checksum and scanner-family coverage receipts bind what was actually examined. Review warnings and incomplete coverage before interpreting a headline result.

entries.topic: retest verify fix finding validated fixed pending deterministic
entries.title: Retest a finding after a fix
entries.content: A retest creates a new server-owned scan; it does not rewrite the original result. A complete deterministic retest can validate that an issue is no longer found within the retested scope. Missing source identity or incomplete coverage stays inconclusive. Engine-only absence does not by itself prove a fix. A finding remains Fixed pending retest until a trusted retest receipt records the outcome.

entries.topic: launch readiness report score assurance ready insufficient evidence
entries.title: Scores, readiness and reports
entries.content: Eligible completed reviews can produce a scoped LyraShield Score and assurance report from retained evidence. Launch readiness can be Insufficient evidence, Ready or Not ready. Ready means no blocking finding was retained within completed scope; it is not certification or proof that untested systems are safe. Inconclusive evidence never becomes green. Reports should be read with their coverage and limitations.

entries.topic: integrations CLI MCP github action coding agent setup
entries.title: Connect LyraShield to developer workflows
entries.content: LyraShield offers a CLI, MCP connection and GitHub Action for supported coding-agent and CI workflows. Follow the guide for the exact client: installation, authentication and runtime permissions differ. A local check-diff is advisory and is not a full recorded scan. Remote OAuth begins read-only unless a browser-confirmed delegated workflow grants specific writes.

entries.topic: pricing plans trial minutes billing packs failed scans charges
entries.title: Where to check current plans and usage
entries.content: The public pricing page has the current Cloud plans, trial terms and minute packs. Signed-in users can see their own subscription, available agent-minutes and usage in Billing. Plan and balance answers should come from the live pricing catalog and account services, not this knowledge entry or an old chat. A failed scan is not billed for agent-minutes.

entries.topic: contact human support request case feedback help
entries.title: Get help from a person
entries.content: If Myra cannot ground an answer or a scan remains blocked, ask Myra to prepare a support case. Review the subject and summary before confirming; the case reference appears after submission. Do not paste credentials or unrelated private data into chat. The public support page also lists support and security-reporting contact paths. Use the helpful or not-helpful rating on an answer to give feedback.

entries.topic: signed in account usage minutes subscription billing balance
entries.title: Check your own account usage
entries.content: For a signed-in account, use the scoped account service or the Billing page to check current plan, agent-minutes and usage. Never ask a visitor to paste account identifiers, payment details or credentials into chat. If the account service is unavailable, say the balance cannot be confirmed and offer a support case.
